deep.reconstruction:
The page belongs to the 1966-67 preparatory notes for the crystals lectures, the material behind 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHES, Dec. 1966; published in Dix exposés, 1968). In characteristic 0, 'cris' here means the infinitesimal site.

Top lines. Differential operators enter 'in a truly natural way'. This is the familiar point that the formal neighbourhoods of the diagonal P^n_{X} are dual to differential operators of order at most n. Grothendieck then flags the analogy between the cosimplicial system of formal neighbourhoods of the diagonals in X^{ν+1} and Čech-Alexander (Alexander-Spanier) cochains: functions on X^{ν+1} near the diagonal play the role of Alexander-Spanier cochains.

§6.5, S = Spec C. Take the Čech covering of the final object of the (infinitesimal/stratifying) topos by X itself. Its Čech nerve is the cosimplicial formal scheme ν ↦ X^{ν+1}_{/X}, the formal completion of X^{ν+1} along the diagonal. This gives a Čech-to-derived spectral sequence
E_2^{pq} = H^p(ν ↦ H^q(X^{ν+1}_{/X}, O)) ⇒ H^*(X_cris, O).
He labels the inner groups 'formal cohomology'.

Write Δ^{(ν)}(i) for the i-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal in X^{ν+1}. If X is proper, each H^q(Δ^{(ν)}(i), O) is finite-dimensional over C. The Mittag-Leffler condition then holds, so formal cohomology is the inverse limit of these groups, and the limit can be pulled outside H^p of the cosimplicial system.

By GAGA each H^q(Δ^{(ν)}(i), O) can be computed analytically. Hence
H^*(X_cris, O) ≅ H^*(X^an_str, O) := H^*(X^an, F^*_{X^an}),
where (next page) F^ν_{X^an} is the sheaf U ↦ Γ(U^{ν+1}_{/U}, O), the analytic formal Čech-Alexander complex.

Next page. He conjectures that for every complex analytic space this complex resolves the constant sheaf C. He deduces that for proper X, H^*(X_strat, O) ≅ H^*(X^an, C).

Purpose: an intrinsic, embedding-free proof that de Rham/infinitesimal (stratifying) cohomology of a possibly singular complex variety is Betti cohomology. The method is to compare via an Alexander-Spanier-type complex of formal neighbourhoods of the diagonal instead of a local embedding into a smooth variety (the Hartshorne approach).
errors: The Čech spectral sequence with E_2 = H^p(ν ↦ H^q(X^{ν+1}_{/X}, O)) computes infinitesimal ('cris') cohomology only if X → final object is a covering. That holds in the infinitesimal topos only when X is smooth over C. For singular X it computes stratifying cohomology. The page writes X_cris on the left but X_str on the right, so this identification needs smoothness or a separate comparison theorem.
Pulling lim_i outside H^p of the cosimplicial system needs Mittag-Leffler at the level of cochain groups (no lim^1 terms). Finite dimensionality guarantees this, but it is only implicit on the page.

Minor: the inputs to GAGA are non-reduced proper schemes Δ^{(ν)}(i). GAGA applies to these, but the identification of the analytic formal completion with lim of analytic infinitesimal neighbourhoods is tacit.

ideas.what: Cohomology of the infinitesimal/stratifying site computed by the cosimplicial system of formal completions of X^{ν+1} along the diagonal, viewed as analogous to Alexander-Spanier cochains
ideas.modern_name: Čech-Alexander complex (formal neighbourhoods of the diagonal); Čech nerve of X → X_dR
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Differential operators arise naturally as duals of the formal neighbourhoods of the diagonal
Passage from formal to finite-level cohomology via Mittag-Leffler and finite dimensionality, then GAGA to go analytic
Analytic stratifying complex F^ν(U) = Γ(U^{ν+1}_{/U}, O) and conjecture that it resolves C for every complex analytic space, hence H^*(X_strat, O) ≅ H^*(X^an, C) for proper X
ideas.modern_name: Formal Poincaré lemma for singular analytic spaces, Alexander-Spanier/Čech nerve version (cf. Hartshorne's algebraic de Rham, Herrera-Lieberman, Bhatt's derived de Rham)
ideas.where_published: The embedding-based comparison H^*(X_inf, O) ≅ H^*(X^an, C) is in the Crystals paper §4; the embedding-free stratifying conjecture is uncertain there

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an embedding-free route to the de Rham-Betti comparison for singular varieties. It uses the stratifying site and the analytic Alexander-Spanier-type complex of formal completions of U^{ν+1} along the diagonal, and reduces everything to the local conjecture that this complex resolves C on any analytic space. I do not know of a published proof or counterexample for this specific complex with O-coefficients. The standard theory (Hartshorne, Bhatt) uses an embedding into a smooth space or derived de Rham instead.
missed.quote: on trouve ainsi H^*(X_cris, O_{X_cris}) ≃ H^*(X^an_str, O_{X^an_str}) =dfn H^*(X^an, F^{an*}_{X^an})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: In derived-algebraic terms this asks whether O-cohomology satisfies descent along the Čech nerve of X → X_dR for singular X. Gaitsgory-Rozenblyum prove such descent for IndCoh/!-pullback (D-modules), not for O. A positive answer, or a counterexample on simple singularities such as a node or cusp, would clarify whether stratifying and infinitesimal cohomology agree in characteristic 0 for singular spaces.

missed.claim: The explicit analogy between formal-neighbourhood Čech complexes and Alexander-Spanier cochains suggests a topological mechanism for the conjecture. Continuous Alexander-Spanier cochains near the diagonal resolve C; the conjecture is the formal-holomorphic analogue. This 'formal Alexander-Spanier' viewpoint was later realized in crystalline and prismatic Čech-Alexander complexes, but is seldom related back to the topological Alexander-Spanier theory.
missed.quote: Analogie avec les cochaînes de Cech-Alexander....
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly expository. It frames de Rham comparison theorems (including prismatic/crystalline Čech-Alexander computations) as formal versions of Alexander-Spanier cohomology.

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is the known Čech-Alexander/GAGA argument from the Crystals paper. The mildly notable content is the attempt to get the comparison for singular X intrinsically via the stratifying site and an analytic local conjecture (stated on the next page). I am unsure this appears in print, and its status for O-coefficients is not standard knowledge.
transcription_corrections: The illegible words after 'suite spectrale de' are likely 'cohomologie de Čech' or 'cohomologie habituelle' (unclear); not 'cohomologie [?]'.

In the final formula the second term is written H^*(X^an_str, O_{X^an_str}) with subscript 'str' (stratifiant), consistent with the next page's 'strat'. The first term's subscript looks like 'X_{str}' / 'X_{strat}' rather than 'X_cris', so the equality may be between stratifying cohomologies, which would remove the first listed error.
